title: OSPF Cost: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: There are two roads to the same city. One is a motorway, and the other a narrow lane. O S P F picks by cost.

lines.t: A motorway and a country lane

scenes.heading: Toll road pricing
scenes.narration: Faster roads are cheaper to use. The cost equals the reference bandwidth divided by the link bandwidth. A hundred megabit link costs one, and a ten megabit link costs ten. You can set a link's cost by hand. Or change the reference, on every router, for fast links.

scenes.heading: Commands
scenes.narration: Three commands to know. Set cost by hand on an interface. Or change the reference bandwidth. And check each interface's cost.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Cost comes from bandwidth, not hops. It uses the configured bandwidth value. Change the reference everywhere or paths will disagree.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva OSPF cost lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Cost is reference bandwidth divided by link bandwidth. Lower cost wins. Match the reference on every router. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva OSPF cost lab.
